diagrams.mechanic_notes: Depicts direct manifold port injection geometry where the injector atomizes fuel directly at the intake valve opening.

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Key layout overview for diagnosing component locations on both Federal and California spec 280Z models.

diagrams.caption: The Fuel Circuit Schematic Diagram
diagrams.description: Schematic flow diagram of the 280Z fuel circuit and related control subsystems, tracing fuel delivery from tank through damper, pump, filter, fuel rail, pressure regulator, and injectors, along with air flow, vacuum sensing, and electrical control signals.

callouts.FUEL FLOW: Solid arrow indicating direction of pressurized gasoline
callouts.AIR FLOW: Open triangle arrow indicating induction air path
callouts.VACUUM: Hollow outline arrow indicating intake manifold vacuum sensing
callouts.POWER SOURCE: Crosshatched pattern line indicating primary electrical feed
callouts.INPUT SIGNAL: Dashed line indicating sensor input to ECU
callouts.OUTPUT SIGNAL: Solid line indicating ECU control command to injectors

diagrams.mechanic_notes: High pressure fuel is constantly supplied to the fuel rail with unused fuel bleeding back to the tank via the pressure regulator; air volume measured at AFM determines base fuel injection duration.

diagrams.caption: FUEL PUMP
diagrams.description: Isometric exterior drawing of the 280Z electric rotary roller fuel pump with mounting bracket and hose fittings.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Wet-type rotary roller fuel pump where gasoline flows around the armature.

diagrams.caption: FUEL PUMP SECTIONAL VIEW
diagrams.description: Longitudinal cutaway sectional view of the electric fuel pump showing internal flow path from inlet, through roller pump mechanism, past electric motor armature, and through outlet check valve, as well as the internal pressure relief valve.

callouts.Inlet: Fuel suction inlet from gas tank
callouts.Relief Valve: Internal pressure relief valve bypassing to inlet
callouts.Motor: Electric motor armature immersed in fuel
callouts.Check Valve: One-way outlet check valve holding line pressure

measurements_and_specs: Relief valve opening pressure: above 43 psi
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Gasoline circulates around the motor armature for cooling and lubrication. Check valve maintains residual fuel system pressure after pump shutdown.

diagrams.caption: FUEL DAMPER
diagrams.description: Exterior view of the fuel pulsation damper showing upper adjusting screw and inlet/outlet tube connections.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Mounted immediately adjacent to the fuel pump near the fuel tank.

diagrams.caption: FUEL DAMPER SECTIONAL VIEW
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional cutaway drawing of the fuel damper revealing the spring-loaded flexible diaphragm that absorbs hydraulic pressure pulses from the roller pump.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Acts as a shock absorber and acoustic muffler to prevent fuel pressure pulsation spikes from reaching injectors or transmitting humming noise into cabin.

diagrams.caption: FUEL FILTER
diagrams.description: Isometric view of the canister-type high-pressure fuel filter showing inlet and outlet tube connections.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: High efficiency filter essential for preventing minuscule contaminants from jamming electronic injector pintles.

diagrams.caption: Fuel filter mounted on the right hand fender panel next to carbon canister
diagrams.description: Illustration of the fuel filter mounted in its bracket on the right hand engine compartment fender panel beside the carbon canister.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Inspect hoses and clamps for leakage whenever replacing filter.

diagrams.caption: INJECTOR
diagrams.description: Exterior view of an electronic fuel injector showing electrical receptacle, braided fuel hose collar, and discharge nozzle.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Solenoid needle valve injector operated by electrical pulses from the ECU.

diagrams.caption: Injectors mounted on the intake manifold
diagrams.description: View of fuel injectors installed on the intake manifold runners adjacent to the cylinder head intake ports with fuel supply rail and wiring harness connectors.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Manifold injection configuration directing fuel spray directly onto intake valves.

diagrams.caption: Injector cross-sectional internal view
diagrams.description: Detailed longitudinal cutaway diagram of the electromagnetic fuel injector detailing all internal operating elements.

callouts.Needle Valve: Magnetic plunger valve sealing against nozzle seat
callouts.Electric Terminal: Electrical plug terminals for ground pulsing
callouts.Filter: Internal fine mesh screen filter at fuel inlet

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Energizing the coil lifts the needle valve against the spring, releasing pressurized fuel through the nozzle orifice.

diagrams.caption: DROPPING RESISTOR
diagrams.description: Exterior view of the dual dropping resistor pack housing with electrical harness plugs.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Contains six individual ballast resistors (one per injector).

diagrams.caption: Dropping resistor location in engine compartment
diagrams.description: Location drawing of the dropping resistor pack mounted on the left inner fender apron forward of the brake master cylinder.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Reduces operating voltage to injectors and protects them against alternator and electrical system voltage spikes.

diagrams.caption: Electronic Control Unit (ECU)
diagrams.description: Isometric drawing of the Electronic Control Unit (ECU) showing metal housing and 35-pin multi-terminal harness receptacle.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: ECU controls fuel delivery duration by switching the ground side of the injector circuits.

diagrams.caption: Testing the fuel injection system at the ECU harness connector with a multimeter
diagrams.description: Diagnostic testing procedure using a multimeter test probes at the 35-pin harness connector in the driver footwell by the pedals.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: The entire EFI electrical circuit and sensor network can be completely tested and diagnosed from the 35-pin connector at the ECU.

diagrams.caption: PRESSURE REGULATOR
diagrams.description: Isometric exterior view of the fuel pressure regulator showing vacuum nipple, fuel inlet lines, and fuel return outlet.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pre-set at factory and non-adjustable.

diagrams.caption: Sectional view of pressure regulator showing spring chamber, diaphragm, and fuel chamber
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional schematic cutaway of the fuel pressure regulator showing vacuum reference chamber, diaphragm, spring, valve seat, and fuel flow paths.

callouts.Spring chamber: Upper reference chamber containing calibrated spring
callouts.Fuel inlet: Dual fuel inlet tubes from fuel rail
callouts.To fuel tank: Return line port back to fuel tank

measurements_and_specs: Differential pressure: 36 psi (between fuel rail and intake manifold)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Maintains a constant 36 psi pressure differential across injector tips by compensating for intake manifold vacuum fluctuations.

diagrams.caption: AIR FLOW METER
diagrams.description: Installation view of the air flow meter mounted in the 280Z engine bay between the air cleaner and throttle chamber.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Measures volume of induction air entering engine; primary load signal for ECU.

diagrams.caption: Throttle Valve operation by throttle linkage
diagrams.description: Illustration showing hand opening the throttle valve butterfly plate on the throttle body via the external throttle actuator linkage.

callouts.Throttle Valve: Rotating throttle valve plate governing induction airflow

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Opening the throttle allows air to flow through AFM and intake manifold, determining engine speed.

diagrams.fig_id: Air Flow Meter Cutaway and Potentiometer
diagrams.caption: Air Flow Meter cutaway view and potentiometer electrical chamber
diagrams.description: Ghosted cutaway and exploded perspective view of the vane-type air flow meter showing the internal flap assembly, helical damping spring, idle bypass channel, air temperature sensor, fuel pump switch contacts, and sealed potentiometer electronics chamber.

callouts.HELICAL SPRING: Calibrated flap return and damping spring
callouts.FLAP (ASSEMBLY): Counterbalanced measuring and damping flap unit
callouts.FUEL PUMP CONTACT POINT: Safety interlock switch contacts for fuel pump power
callouts.POTENTIOMETER: Linear resistive potentiometer track and wiper arm

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Air pushing the flap rotates the potentiometer wiper to supply a proportional voltage signal to the ECU. Also houses the fuel pump safety interlock switch.

diagrams.caption: Air Flow Meter internal electrical circuit schematic
diagrams.description: Internal circuit diagram of the air flow meter showing the stepped resistor ladder potentiometer (terminals 9, 8, 7, 6), intake air temperature sensor thermistor (terminal 27), and fuel pump safety contacts (terminals 36, 39).
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Contacts 36 and 39 close as soon as induction air deflects the flap, energizing the fuel pump relay during engine run.

diagrams.caption: IDLE SPEED SCREW
diagrams.description: Adjustment procedure showing a screwdriver turning the idle speed bypass screw on the throttle chamber.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Controls idle engine speed by regulating bypass air volume around the closed throttle plate. WARNING: ANY VACUUM LEAK between AFM and intake valves will alter idle speed and lean out the mixture.

diagrams.caption: ELECTRONIC FUEL INJECTION SYSTEM (ELECTRONIC SIGNAL)
diagrams.description: Block schematic showing all input sensor signals wired to the Electronic Control Unit (ECU): Ignition coil (RPM trigger), Throttle valve switch (Idle/Full throttle), Water temperature sensor, Air flow meter (Potentiometer, Air temp sensor, Fuel pump switch), Ignition switch (Start signal), and Battery.

callouts.THROTTLE VALVE POSITION SIGNAL: Idle and full load contact signals to ECU
callouts.AIR TEMPERATURE SIGNAL: Intake air temperature resistance to ECU
callouts.POTENTIOMETER SIGNAL: AFM flap angle voltage to ECU
callouts.START SIGNAL: Ignition switch start position feed to ECU
callouts.FUEL PUMP CONTACT POINTS: AFM internal switch to fuel pump relay

measurements_and_specs: Simultaneous injection: all 6 injectors fire once per revolution (twice per 4-stroke cycle)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Ignition coil negative hookup serves as both engine speed tachometer input and injection timing trigger.

diagrams.caption: Throttle Switch mounted on throttle chamber
diagrams.description: Drawing of the throttle valve switch mounted on the side of the throttle body, coupled to the throttle valve shaft.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Contains two distinct sets of contact points: idle contacts and full throttle contacts.

diagrams.caption: Throttle switch internal contact points: Full Throttle Contact Points and Idle Contact Points
diagrams.description: Internal view of the throttle switch revealing the rotating contact cam, idle contact points, and full throttle contact points.

callouts.Full Throttle Contact Points: Upper contacts closed when throttle is opened wide
callouts.Idle Contact Points: Lower contacts closed when throttle is released to idle

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Idle switch closes when accelerator pedal is released, signaling idle enrichment or deceleration fuel cut depending on engine RPM.

diagrams.caption: Engine RPM thresholds for fuel cut during deceleration: 3200 rpm fuel injection stops, 2800 rpm fuel injection begins, 800 rpm idling
diagrams.description: Vertical chart showing engine RPM thresholds for deceleration fuel cut-off and resumption.

callouts.2800 rpm: FUEL INJECTION BEGINS (injection resumes as RPM falls to 2800)

diagrams.mechanic_notes: When decelerating with idle contacts closed, ECU shuts off injector pulses completely between 3200 rpm and 2800 rpm for emissions control and fuel economy.

diagrams.caption: Water Temperature Sensor and its location in the thermostat housing
diagrams.description: Component drawing of the threaded water temperature sensor alongside its installation location in the front thermostat housing.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Senses engine coolant temperature to determine warm-up enrichment.

diagrams.caption: AIR TEMPERATURE SENSOR in the air flow meter inlet
diagrams.description: Close-up perspective of the air flow meter inlet horn showing the location of the intake air temperature sensor thermistor bulb.

callouts.Air Temperature Sensor: Thermistor bead positioned directly in incoming air stream

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Below 68°F, ECU meters extra fuel to compensate for denser cold intake air. Eliminates need for carbureted-style exhaust manifold preheat tubes.

diagrams.caption: COLD START VALVE
diagrams.description: Exterior view of the cold start valve showing 2-bolt mounting flange, electrical receptacle, and fuel supply nipple.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Seventh injector providing cold cranking fuel enrichment.

diagrams.caption: SECTIONAL VIEW OF COLD START VALVE
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional cutaway drawing of the cold start valve showing internal electrical terminal, fuel inlet, solenoid magnet coil, plunger valve, and swirl spray nozzle.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Operates ONLY while ignition starter is cranking; sprays atomized fuel into intake plenum.

diagrams.fig_id: Cold Start Valve - Thermotime Switch Schematic
diagrams.caption: COLD START VALVE — THERMOTIME SWITCH SCHEMATIC
diagrams.description: Electrical schematic illustrating the series circuit connecting ignition 'Start' terminal, cold start valve solenoid, and the thermotime switch bimetal heater and contacts to ground.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Prevents engine flooding by limiting cold start valve injection time to a maximum of approximately 12 seconds during extended cranking.

diagrams.caption: THERMOTIME SWITCH in thermostat housing
diagrams.description: Perspective drawing of the thermostat housing assembly showing the thermotime switch screwed in next to the water temperature sensor.

callouts.THERMOTIME SWITCH: Threaded thermotime switch with electrical connector

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Engine coolant temperature determines initial bimetal deflection; if coolant is warm, contacts remain open and prevent cold start valve injection entirely.

diagrams.caption: AIR REGULATOR
diagrams.description: Isometric view of the auxiliary air regulator assembly showing air bypass tubes, 2-pin electrical connector, and mounting bracket.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Provides fast idle air during engine warm-up by bypassing throttle valve.

diagrams.caption: SECTIONAL VIEW OF AIR REGULATOR
diagrams.description: Cutaway sectional view of the auxiliary air regulator detailing the rotating shutter plate, bimetallic arm, electric heater winding, and air passages.

callouts.Shutter: Rotary shutter disc that progressively closes air aperture
callouts.Air inlet: Bypass air intake from upstream of throttle
callouts.Air outlet: Bypass air delivery into intake manifold
callouts.Heater: Electrical heating coil powered while engine runs
callouts.Electric terminal (Current when engine i: Connector pins receiving power from fuel pump circuit
callouts.Bimetal: Bimetal strip deflecting as heater warms to close shutter

wiring_and_connections: Electric terminal: current when engine is running
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Not controlled by ECU or cold start valve; heater is powered whenever fuel pump runs, gradually closing shutter to reduce idle speed to normal.

callouts.AIR FLOW METER: Internal potentiometer, temperature sensor, and pump contacts (pins 39, 36, 6, 8, 9, 7, 27)
callouts.THROTTLE VALVE SWITCH: Idle, full throttle, and ground terminals (pins 3, 18, 2)

wiring_and_connections: Terminals 39, 36: Fuel pump interlock contacts in AFM
Pins 14, 15, 30, 31, 32, 33: Injector ground triggers from ECU
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Critical reference diagram for tracing wiring faults, checking pin continuity, and testing sensor voltages from the 35-pin ECU disconnect plug.

diagrams.caption: Fuel Injection Harness routing through engine compartment and cabin
diagrams.description: Vehicle isometric drawing illustrating the dedicated layout and body routing path of the separate EFI wiring harness connecting the battery, engine sensors/actuators, firewall passthrough grommet, and ECU in the driver footwell.
wiring_and_connections: Isolated EFI wiring harness separate from vehicle chassis harness
diagrams.mechanic_notes: The EFI harness is independent of the vehicle's standard chassis wiring, featuring positive-locking connector plugs to prevent intermittent electrical faults. All circuits converge at the 35-pin ECU plug.

diagrams.caption: Fuel Injection Relay assembly
diagrams.description: Perspective view of the fuel injection dual relay assembly showing mounting bracket and terminal spade connectors.
wiring_and_connections: 6-pin / multiple spade terminals on relay base
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Contains two internal relays: Power Relay and Fuel Pump Relay.

diagrams.caption: Fuel injection relay mounting on left hand kick panel above control unit
diagrams.description: Illustration of the driver side footwell / left hand kick panel area showing the fuel injection relay mounted with two screws to the bracket above the EFI ECU control unit.
wiring_and_connections: Harness connector to fuel injection relay
Main EFI harness routing above kick panel
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Located on the left-hand kick panel directly above the EFI Electronic Control Unit (ECU).

diagrams.description: Internal schematic of the fuel injection relay with the Power Relay section shaded/highlighted, illustrating circuit connections to battery, ignition switch, injectors, ECU, and AFM contacts.

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Sends current directly from battery to fuel pump and auxiliary air regulator heater.

diagrams.description: Schematic diagram showing current paths (indicated by arrows) during cranking: key in START position energizes both the power relay and the fuel pump relay simultaneously.

callouts.POWER TO: 1. CONTROL UNIT 2. AIR FLOW ME: Power To: 1. Control Unit, 2. Air Flow Meter Pump Contacts
callouts.FROM AIR FLOW METER PUMP CONTACTS: From Air Flow Meter Pump Contacts

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Both relays energize directly from the starter signal to guarantee fuel pressure and ECU power during cranking.

diagrams.caption: POWER RELAY: IGNITION ON circuit flow
diagrams.description: Schematic diagram showing current flow path with key in ON position: power relay coil remains energized from IGN SW ON terminal, while fuel pump relay contacts remain open until AFM flap moves.

callouts.POWER TO: 1. CONTROL UNIT 2. AIR FLOW ME: Power To: 1. Control Unit, 2. Air Flow Meter Pump Contacts
callouts.FROM AIR FLOW METER PUMP CONTACTS: From Air Flow Meter Pump Contacts

wiring_and_connections: Current flows from IGN SW 'ON' terminal to power relay coil and ground
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Key ON energizes power relay continuously, supplying power to ECU, injectors, and AFM switch terminals.

diagrams.caption: Air Flow Meter internal mechanism showing flap, potentiometer, and fuel pump contact points
diagrams.description: Cutaway illustration of the air flow meter assembly detailing internal components: air measuring flap valve, return helical spring, idle air bypass channel, intake air temperature thermistor, potentiometer board, and fuel pump switch contact points.
wiring_and_connections: Internal contacts wired to AFM connector terminals for fuel pump relay trigger
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Flap must swing freely. Air flow moves flap against helical spring to mechanically close the fuel pump switch contacts.

diagrams.caption: FUEL PUMP RELAY: ENGINE RUNNING circuit flow
diagrams.description: Schematic diagram showing current paths when engine is running: power flows from power relay through closed AFM contacts into the fuel pump relay coil, energizing fuel pump and air regulator.

callouts.POWER TO: 1. CONTROL UNIT 2. AIR FLOW ME: Power To: 1. Control Unit, 2. Air Flow Meter Pump Contacts
callouts.FROM AIR FLOW METER PUMP CONTACTS: From Air Flow Meter Pump Contacts

wiring_and_connections: Current from power relay passes through AFM switch contacts to fuel pump relay coil and ground
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Diode in fuel pump relay prevents backfeed into starter solenoid line during engine running.

diagrams.caption: Electronic fuel injection harness, battery, relays, and ECU connector routing
diagrams.description: Ghosted cutaway view of 280Z chassis showing complete EFI wire harness runs between battery, engine sensors/injectors, dropping resistor, relays, and ECU in the driver footwell.
wiring_and_connections: Main wiring harness running along inner fender and firewall to driver side kick panel ECU
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Always check all electrical harness connectors for loose fit and terminal corrosion before diagnosing individual components.

diagrams.caption: Vacuum hose and intake leakage inspection locations
diagrams.description: Isometric cutaway view of engine compartment highlighting vacuum hoses, rubber intake boots, and PCV connections that must be checked for cracks and vacuum leaks.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Inspect all rubber hoses for hardening, splitting, or loose clamps. Vacuum leaks cause lean running and erratic idle.

diagrams.caption: Checking air leakage in air intake system
diagrams.description: Comprehensive schematic cross-section of the complete induction and crankcase breathing system illustrating all 26 potential points of unmetered air leakage downstream of the air flow meter.

callouts.7: Injector mounting surface in intake manifold
callouts.8: Cylinder head mounting surface in intake manifold
callouts.9: Hose (throttle chamber to 3-way connector), both sides
callouts.10: Hose (3-way connector to rocker cover), both sides
callouts.11: Hose (3-way connector to air regulator), both sides
callouts.12: Hose (air regulator to throttle chamber connector), both sides
callouts.14: Hose (pipe connector to P.C.V. valve), both sides
callouts.22: E.G.R. valve mounting surface (California models only)
callouts.25: Oil seal (on front and rear of crankshaft)

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Because the EFI system measures airflow entering the engine, ANY unmetered air entering through vacuum hoses, dipstick O-ring, oil cap seal, or crank seals causes severe lean misfire or rough idle.

diagrams.caption: Locating ignition lead wire to control unit next to power relay
diagrams.description: Drawing showing kick panel area with arrow pointing to the inline bullet connector of the ignition trigger lead wire adjacent to the power relay bracket.
wiring_and_connections: Ignition signal input bullet connector leading to ECU pin 1
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Check for 12V test light illumination with ignition switch in ON position.

diagrams.caption: Listening to injector operation with mechanic's stethoscope or screwdriver
diagrams.description: Technician using a screwdriver held against a fuel injector nozzle with ear against handle to listen for audible clicking during simulated ignition triggering.
measurements_and_specs: Audible click expected every third break of ignition lead wire
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Disconnecting and reconnecting ignition lead wire simulates distributor ignition pulse; ECU should trigger injectors on every 3rd pulse.

diagrams.caption: Inspecting and disconnecting cold start valve electrical harness connector
diagrams.description: Hand disconnecting electrical quick-disconnect connector from the cold start valve on the intake manifold.
wiring_and_connections: Cold start valve two-terminal harness connector
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Depress wire retaining spring clip when unplugging connector. Cranking voltage must be at least 9.6V to operate cold start enrichment.

diagrams.caption: Thermotime switch connector location on thermostat housing
diagrams.description: Arrow pointing to the thermotime switch electrical connector located on the thermostat housing alongside the water temperature sensor and thermal transmitter.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: If thermotime switch contacts stick closed when hot, engine floods due to unwanted cold start valve operation.

diagrams.caption: Locating ignition lead wire connector near power relay
diagrams.description: Kick panel area drawing indicating the bullet connector for the ECU ignition trigger input wire next to the relay bracket.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Check for 12V current with test light when ignition is ON.

diagrams.caption: Listening for injector clicking with screwdriver to ear
diagrams.description: Technician with handle of screwdriver pressed to ear and blade against fuel injector to listen for injector solenoid clicking while triggering circuit.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Injectors should click every 3rd pulse.

diagrams.caption: Testing air flow meter fuel pump contacts by manually opening the flap
diagrams.description: Hand reaching into inlet collar of air flow meter and manually pushing the flap valve open to test activation of the internal fuel pump contacts.
wiring_and_connections: Internal fuel pump switch contacts wired to AFM pins
diagrams.mechanic_notes: With ignition ON, moving flap even slightly should immediately activate the electric fuel pump. If engine starts and immediately dies when key returns to ON, defective AFM contacts are a primary cause.

diagrams.caption: Checking auxiliary air regulator by pinching off hose with pliers
diagrams.description: View of intake manifold and auxiliary air regulator hoses showing pliers pinching the rubber air hose to test for internal regulator shutter leakage at warm idle.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: When engine is warmed up, pinching the air regulator hose should NOT cause idle speed to drop. If idle drops, regulator is failing to close completely (heater circuit defect or sticking shutter).

diagrams.caption: Checking air flow meter flap for smooth mechanical movement
diagrams.description: Technician using a finger to push the air flow meter flap through its full travel to confirm completely unrestricted mechanical movement.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Flap must swing freely without sticking, catching, or dragging against the meter housing throughout its entire range of motion.

diagrams.caption: Testing air flow meter flap for resistance points causing hesitation
diagrams.description: Close-up of hand pushing the AFM measuring flap to detect subtle drag or binding points that cause hesitation on throttle tip-in.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: If any resistance points or catching is felt, replace the air flow meter.

diagrams.caption: Fuel pressure gauge installed in fuel line to cold start valve
diagrams.description: Drawing showing dial fuel pressure test gauge tee'd into the fuel delivery hose connected to the cold start valve on the intake manifold.
measurements_and_specs: Fuel pressure test: Refer to 280Z Service Manual page EF-57
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Connect pressure gauge between fuel delivery pipe and cold start valve. Excessive pressure causes rich running and high CO emissions.

diagrams.caption: Checking air flow meter flap smoothness for surge conditions
diagrams.description: Technician checking AFM flap deflection for mechanical stiffness or flat spots that induce cruising surge.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Verify flap swings freely with smooth resistance from internal spring.

diagrams.caption: Testing harness circuits with multimeter at 35-pin ECU connector
diagrams.description: Technician using multimeter test probes to probe specific pin sockets on the disconnected 35-pin control unit wiring harness plug in the footwell area.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Disconnect 35-pin connector only with ignition OFF. Insert probes gently into terminal cavities to avoid damaging spring tension.

diagrams.caption: Complete EFI wiring schematic highlighting Test #1 - (1): Idle Throttle Switch circuit (pins 2 and 18)
diagrams.description: System-wide EFI wiring schematic highlighting the idle contact circuit of the throttle valve switch connected between pin 2 and ground return pin 18 at the 35-pin control unit connector.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Turn off ignition before disconnecting ECU. Check for continuity when throttle is at idle stop; opening throttle slightly must break continuity.

diagrams.caption: 35-pin ECU connector pin assignment showing test pins 2 and 18 highlighted
diagrams.description: Face-view pinout of the 35-pin female control unit harness connector highlighting pin 2 and pin 18.
measurements_and_specs: Connect ohmmeter leads between pin 2 and pin 18
wiring_and_connections: Upper row pins 1 through 18, lower row pins 19 through 35
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pin 2 is on top row near left; pin 18 is far right on top row.

diagrams.caption: Test #1 - (2): Full Throttle Switch Circuit Schematic
diagrams.description: Schematic of the 280Z EFI wiring harness highlighting the throttle valve switch circuit across pins 3 and 18 connected to the 35-pin control unit connector.

callouts.3: Throttle valve switch full throttle contact

troubleshooting.symptom: Difficult fuel pump priming after running out of fuel
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Rotary roller 'wet' type fuel pump drained of fuel and cannot pull suction head
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Fill fuel tank completely to the top before cranking so fuel gravity-primes the pump

troubleshooting.symptom: Cylinder misfire, rough running, or erratic injection
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Contaminants lodged in precision injector nozzle or internal screen due to depleted filter
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace high-pressure fuel filter (normal service interval 25,000 miles)

troubleshooting.symptom: Erratic idle speed, rough idle, or improper air-fuel mixture ratio
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Vacuum leak between air flow meter and intake valves allowing unmetered air to bypass flap
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Inspect and seal all rubber intake ducts, throttle body gaskets, auxiliary air hoses, and manifold joints

troubleshooting.symptom: Engine flooding during extended cold cranking
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Cold start valve remaining open or defective thermotime switch failing to open internal contacts
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check thermotime switch bimetal heater and contacts (must open and interrupt cold start valve ground within 12 seconds)

troubleshooting.symptom: Engine Will Not Start
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Ignition system fault; manifold vacuum leaks; fuel pump/pressure regulator inoperative; missing ignition trigger input to ECU; faulty power relay or ECU
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check hot spark from coil; inspect PCV, dipstick, oil cap, AFM hoses for leaks; check fuel pump operation and regulator buzzing in START position; test ignition lead wire for 12V; test injector clicking every 3rd pulse; perform circuit tests 1-(6), 1-(3a-3c), 3-(3), 1-(5), 3-(1), 3-(2); test power relay

troubleshooting.symptom: Engine Hard To Start Only When Cold
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Low battery cranking voltage (< 9.6V); cold start valve inoperative; cold start circuit 3-(3) wiring fault; defective thermotime switch
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check battery voltage while cranking (must be >= 9.6V); perform circuit check 3-(3); perform cold start valve component test (EF-54)

troubleshooting.symptom: Engine Hard To Start Only When Hot (Above 170°F)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Cold start valve leaking or operating when engine hot (flooding); defective thermotime switch sticking closed; fuel vapor lock or improper fuel pressure; leaking injectors; water temp sensor fault
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Disconnect cold start valve, clear flooded fuel, and crank; if engine starts easily, disconnect thermotime switch to isolate whether valve or switch is defective; perform circuit test 1-(6), 1-(3a-3c), fuel pressure test, and injector leakage test

troubleshooting.symptom: Engine Starts, Then Stalls
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective air flow meter fuel pump switch contacts; missing ignition signal input; power relay not holding in ON position; water temperature sensor circuit fault; defective auxiliary air regulator
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Verify ignition lead wire has 12V in ON; listen for injector clicking; check power relay clicks twice (ON and START); push open AFM flap with ignition ON to test fuel pump run; perform circuit test 1-(6) and check auxiliary air regulator

troubleshooting.symptom: Engine Idles Too Fast — Cannot Be Adjusted With Speed Screw Or Engine Idle Is Unstable
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Auxiliary air regulator stuck open or heater circuit open; throttle plate not closing fully; sticking EGR valve; B.C.D.D. valve open at idle; manifold vacuum leaks (PCV, dipstick, oil cap, AFM boots); throttle valve switch out of adjustment
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Pinch off auxiliary air regulator hose with pliers: if idle drops, test circuit 1-(8) or replace regulator; check throttle plate stop; check EGR valve seating; check BCDD relief solenoid; check intake for false air leaks; perform circuit tests 1-(1) through 1-(8)

troubleshooting.symptom: Engine Misfires — HC Reading Too High
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Ignition system defect; voltage regulator over/under-charging; loose or corroded harness connectors; clogged fuel filter or tank strainer; leaking/dirty injectors; faulty ECU internal connection
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check ignition thoroughly; check charging system voltage; disconnect, inspect, and clean all EFI connectors; check fuel supply circuit for blockage; tap ECU while driving to check for intermittent internal fault; check fuel pressure (EF-57); perform circuit tests

troubleshooting.symptom: Engine Will Not Rev. — Lack Of Power
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Transistor ignition pickup coil or coil failure; throttle plate not opening fully; AFM flap sticking or binding mechanically; fuel filter or tank strainer restricted; low fuel pressure; full throttle switch or AFM circuit faults
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check transistor ignition pickup coils; verify throttle linkage reaches full wide open; remove intake boot and verify AFM flap opens fully and smoothly by hand; check fuel filter/lines; perform fuel pressure test; perform circuit tests 1-(2), 2-(1), 2-(2), 2-(3a-3f), 1-(3a-3c), 1-(1), 1-(4), 1-(6), 1-(8)

troubleshooting.symptom: Hesitation — Stumble On Acceleration
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Air flow meter flap sticking or encountering mechanical resistance; unmetered intake air/vacuum leaks; low fuel pressure; throttle switch transition fault
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Remove intake hose from AFM and check flap movement with finger; replace AFM if any resistance or binding is felt; check intake manifold and PCV hoses for leaks; check fuel pressure; perform complete circuit tests

troubleshooting.symptom: Poor Gas Mileage, Or CO Reading Too High
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Incorrect ignition timing / weak spark; clogged air cleaner; excessive fuel pressure; defective water temperature sensor (enrichment on continuously); air temperature sensor fault; leaking cold start valve; dirty injectors
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check timing and spark energy; inspect air cleaner element; tee in pressure gauge at cold start valve to check fuel pressure; perform circuit tests 1-(6), 1-(4), 1-(1), 1-(2), 1-(3a-3c), 3-(2), 1-(8), 2-(3a-3f)

troubleshooting.symptom: Surge
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Mechanical binding or uneven resistance in air flow meter flap; manifold vacuum leaks; intermittent throttle switch or AFM resistor track wear
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check AFM flap for smoothness of operation; inspect PCV valve, dipstick seal, oil cap seal, and manifold gaskets; perform circuit tests 1-(1), 1-(2), 1-(3a-3c), 1-(5), 1-(9a-9d), 1-(4), 1-(6), 1-(8), 2-(1), 2-(2), 2-(3a-3f)

troubleshooting.symptom: Backfiring
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Intake manifold vacuum leaks; lean air-fuel mixture; defective idle/full throttle switch; water temp sensor open circuit; injector circuit fault
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check for manifold vacuum leaks (PCV, dipstick, oil cap, AFM hoses); perform circuit tests 1-(1), 1-(2), 1-(3a-3c), 1-(4), 1-(6), 2-(1), 2-(2), 2-(3a-3f)

troubleshooting.symptom: Afterfire Or Afterburning (Exhaust Popping)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Throttle valve switch misadjusted (idle contact not closing during deceleration); rich fuel mixture or leaking injector; ignition timing/spark defect; start signal circuit remaining energized
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Perform circuit tests 1-(1) (idle switch), 1-(2), 1-(3a-3c), 1-(4), 1-(6), 2-(3a-3f), and 3-(1) ('Start' signal circuit); check throttle switch adjustment (EF-65)

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Full Throttle Switch Test #1-(2)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective throttle valve switch or wiring fault
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Throttle Valve Switch (1975 280Z Service Manual, page EF-56); check Wiring (page EF-26).

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Air Flow Meter Resistance #1 Test #1-(3a)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective air flow meter potentiometer or harness wiring fault
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Air Flow Meter (page EF-51); check Wiring (page EF-27).

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Air Flow Meter Resistance #2 Test #1-(3b)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective air flow meter slider/resistor track or wiring fault
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Air Flow Meter (page EF-51); check Wiring (page EF-28).

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Air Flow Meter Resistance #3 Test #1-(3c)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective air flow meter potentiometer resistor or wiring fault
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Air Flow Meter (page EF-51); check Wiring (page EF-29).

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Air Temperature Sensor Resistance Test #1-(4)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective air temperature thermistor in air flow meter or wiring fault
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Air Temperature Sensor (page EF-52); check Wiring (page EF-30).

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Air Flow Meter Fuel Pump Contacts Test #1-(5)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective internal fuel pump contacts in air flow meter or wiring open
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Fuel Pump Contact Points (page EF-52); check Wiring (page EF-31).

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Water Temperature Sensor Resistance Test #1-(6)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective cylinder head water temperature sensor or harness open/short
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Water Temperature Sensor (page EF-52, 53); check Wiring (page EF-32).

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Fuel Pump Relay Circuit Test #1-(7)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective fuel injection relay or wiring open
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Fuel Injection Relay (page EF-54); check Wiring (page EF-33).

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Air Regulator and Fuel Pump Circuit Test #1-(8)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective air regulator heater, faulty fuel pump, or open harness wiring
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Air Regulator (page EF-58); check Fuel Pump (page EF-56); check Wiring (page EF-34).

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Control Unit Ground Circuit #1 Test #1-9(a)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Faulty harness ground connection at pin 5
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Wiring Harness (page EF-35).

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Control Unit Ground Circuit #2 Test #1-9(b)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Faulty harness ground connection at pin 16
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Wiring Harness (page EF-36).

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Control Unit Ground Circuit #3 Test #1-9(c)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Faulty harness ground connection at pin 17
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Wiring Harness (page EF-37).

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Control Unit Ground Circuit #4 Test #1-9(d)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Faulty harness ground connection at pin 35
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Wiring Harness (page EF-38).

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Ignition Coil Trigger Input Circuit Test #2-(1)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective ignition coil trigger circuit, open ballast/resistor, or poor in-line connector contact
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Ignition Input Circuit (page EF-39); check In-Line Harness Connector (page EF-40).

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Control Unit Power Input Circuit Test #2-(2)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Inoperative EFI power relay, blown fusible link, or open wiring
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Power Relay (page EF-54); check Wiring (page EF-40).

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory #4 Injector Circuit Test #2-3(a)

troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Wiring (page EF-41); check Dropping Resistor (page EF-56); check Relay (page EF-54); check Injector (page EF-57).

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective air regulator heater, faulty relay contact, or open wiring

troubleshooting.symptom: Unsatisfactory Cold Start System Circuit Test #3-(3)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective cold start valve, inoperative thermotime switch, faulty relay, or wiring fault
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check Cold Start Valve (page EF-54); check Thermotime Switch (page EF-53); check Relay (page EF-54); check Wiring (page EF-49).

troubleshooting.symptom: Engine Will Not Start (Component Checks)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Inoperative injectors, relay failure, failed control unit, stuck/faulty air flow meter, low/improper fuel pressure, leaking injectors, or leaking cold start valve
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Perform component checks per 1975 280Z Service Manual: Injector Sound (EF-57), Relay (EF-54), Control Unit Replacement (EF-51), AFM Flap Operation (EF-51), AFM Resistance/Voltage Meas. (EF-52), Fuel Pressure Test (EF-56/7), Injector Leakage (EF-57), Cold Start Valve Leakage (EF-54), Pressure Regulator (EF-57).

troubleshooting.symptom: Idle Too High Or Too Rough (Component Checks)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Faulty injector operation, improper fuel pressure, leaking injectors, cold start valve leakage, or defective fuel pressure regulator
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Perform component checks per 1975 280Z Service Manual: Injector Sound (EF-57), Fuel Pressure Test (EF-56/7), Injector Leakage (EF-57), Cold Start Valve Leakage (EF-54), Pressure Regulator (EF-57).

troubleshooting.symptom: Engine Misfires — HC Reading Too High (Component Checks)

troubleshooting.corrective_action: Perform component checks per 1975 280Z Service Manual: Injector Sound (EF-57), Auxiliary Air Regulator (EF-58), Control Unit Replacement (EF-51), AFM Flap Operation (EF-51), AFM Resistance/Voltage Meas. (EF-52), Fuel Pressure Test (EF-56/7), Pressure Regulator (EF-57).
